headline: Approved June minutes; no regular August meeting; IT department to be invited to a future discussion of the Discrimination Reporting Form.
summary: Members heard a presentation about Salem LUCE, a hotline that verifies reported ICE presence in the community. They discussed changes to the Discrimination Reporting Form and noted the city was not selected for a state grant. There will be no regular August meeting.

Agreed by consensus to invite someone from the IT department to a future meeting to discuss the Discrimination Reporting Form.
Continued the marketing campaign discussion until Chair Zaragoza Frey is present at a meeting.

MINUTES OF THE RACE EQUITY COMMISSION 
July 16, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Salem Race Equity Commission (REC) was held on July 16, 2026, at 
5:00 pm via Zoom, an online video conference call system in accordance with Chapter 2 
of the Act of 2025. Pursuant to Section 30A of chapter 20 of the acts of 2021, as amended 
by 2 section 40 of chapter 2 of the acts of 2023, and further amended by Section 1 o f 
Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2025, the City is authorized to conduct remote meetings of its 
public bodies through June 30, 2027. 
 
 
1. Roll Call 
 
Present on the call were: Regina Zaragoza Frey (Chair), Dr. Shelby Ortega (Vice Chair) 
Alexandra Ramos, Rosa Alvarado, Jennifer Winsor, Dr. Melanie Sonsteng -Person, Dr. 
Vanita Naidoo, Human Resources Director Lisa Cammarata, Chief of Police Lucas Miller. 
 
Absent were: Chief of Police Lucas Miller, Salem Public Schools Acting Superintendent 
Kate Carbone, and City Council Liaison Kyle Davis 
 
 
2. Approve previous meeting minutes. 
 
a. June 4, 2026 
 
VOTE: Motion to approve the meeting minutes for June 4, 2026 was made by Lisa 
Cammarata, seconded by Alexandra Ramos, and the motion was carried 
unanimously by roll call vote. 
 
 
3. Public Comment. 
 
Chair Zaragoza made a call for public comment. There was no public comment. 
 
 
4. Announcements and Updates

a. Progress on grant applications: Regina to provide an update from Kerry 
Murphy, Health and Wellness Coordinator, regarding the MA Community 
Health and Healthy Aging Funds grant application. 
 
This was a major grant that would have allowed the committee to do a lot of work 
in racial equity in relation to ageism for the next few years. Unfortunately, the City 
of Salem was not selected as a recipient. Chair Zaragoza Frey had reviewed the 
application and it was a strong application. So Chair Zaragoza Frey is working with 
Kerry Murphy and other staff to identify other sources of funding to continue the 
“Salem for All Ages” initiatives. Chair Zaragoza Frey also serves on this committee 
and believes there is a lot of overlap between both committees and that there will 
be upcoming opportunities for collaboration.  
 
b. Commission Membership Updates. Introduction of Dr. Javier Garcia-Perez. 
 
Welcome Dr. Javier Garcia -Perez! Dr. Garcia -Perez introduced himself. He has 
lived in the City for one year and is a professor of social work at Salem State 
University. Other members introduced themselves as well. 
 
Another membership update: Colby Bomberowitz had to step back from his 
position due to scheduling conflicts. Chair Zaragoza Frey encouraged members to 
connect her with any residents who may be interested in serving. 
 
c. August Meeting Schedule: Discussion of replacing the regular August meeting 
with an informal Commission gathering. 
 
There will not be a regular August meeting. Instead, members will be invited to an 
informal gathering of REC members so everyone can get to know each other 
outside of the formal meetings. Chair Zaragoza Frey will follow up over email with 
additional details. 
 
d. Upcoming City Council discussion on City Seal. 
 
The City Seal discussion started in REC meetings so Chair Zaragoza Frey shared 
that the City Council will be taking up a discussion and potential vote on this topic 
during their meeting on August 25. 
 
5. Presentation and discussion from local Salem LUCE network leader, Julia Scherer -
Hook: Introduction to Salem LUCE.

MAYOR

Julia Scherer -Hook presented about Salem LUCE. LUCE is a hotline that does rapid 
response verification of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) presence in a 
community. Anyone can call the hotline to report something then LUCE dispatches people 
to verify if it is ICE or what exactly is happening then send the information back to the 
community. The slides presented included the following information: 
 
● Goals 
○ Give the immigrant community in Massachusetts a feeling of real support, 
organizing, and concrete assistance with dignity. 
○ Create opportunities to make visible the otherwise invisible attacks on our 
communities, and their heart wrenching costs. 
○ Create opportunities to go on the offensive against those who attack. 
○ Connect people to local and statewide organizing efforts. 
○ Maintain an identity statewide which is trustworthy, reliable, consistent, 
reassuring, and that people can go to for accurate information. 
● LUCE Theory of Change 
○ Ice agents want to operate in the shadows. They want people to be afraid. 
○ When we verify ICE presence, we are able to share information; 
■ Community members can make informed decisions. 
■ Provide witness/protective presence on site. 
■ Decreases likelihood of violence/illegal activity. 
○ When we verify that it is NOT ICE, we help stop harmful rumors. 
● Allies Organizing in Solidarity: 
○ Solidarity – LUCE is an immigrant centered immigrant led organizations. 
○ Allies play key roles as verifiers. 
○ No saviors – we are all in this together, although we are not experiencing 
violence in the same way. 
● On Criminalization of Immigration 
○ We do not throw people under the bus - we fight for everyone’s freedom - 
all people who have been criminalized, policed, been in prison. 
○ “Good” vs “bad” immigrant narratives seek to further divide and pit people 
against each other. 
● Psychological Torture 
○ The feat is the tactic. The fear allows corporations to exploit immigrant 
workers.  
○ They want to create the feeling that they are everywhere, and there is 
nothing we can do. 
○ There are more of us than there are of them.
DOMINICK PANGALLO 
MAYOR 
CITY OF SALEM 
RACE EQUITY COMMISSION 
  
98 WASHINGTON STREET 
SALEM, MASSACHUSETTS 01970 
 978.745-9595 X. 41505 
 
 
 
 
 
REGINA ZARAGOZA FREY, CHAIR 
SHELBY ORTEGA, VICE CHAIR 
 
● Needs of Rapid Response 
○ During ICE activity, we record and document for these simple and serious 
goals: 
■ Reduce or eliminate harm to people in custody or in the community. 
■ Prevent escalation that could direct violence toward them or others. 
■ Ensure names, information, and family contacts are captured so no 
one is disappeared. 
■ Connect impacted families to legal resources and support. 
○ Any tactic that undermines these goals, even symbolically, must be 
reconsidered. 
● Why Whistles Undermine Those Goals 
○ Whistles do not increase safety in our specific context. They: 
■ Could make it harder to document and capture information. 
■ Escalate already volatile ICE agents who don’t respect our rights. 
■ Increase the likelihood of aggression toward bystanders or the 
detained person. 
■ Create confusion for community members and children, while 
having reduced utility in a suburban terrain. 
○ Loudness does not equal effectiveness. 
● What We Have Accomplished Statewide 
○ 7,000+ calls to the hotline from February to December 2025 
○ Most frequently spoken languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese, Haitian 
Creole 
○ 79% Response Rate 
○ LUCE encountered ICE 430 times in 74 towns. 
○ 40 verifier “hubs” across the state 
● LUCE on the North Shore 
○ 3 hubs with verifiers who go out into these communities 
○ Cape Ann Hub: Gloucester, Rockport, Manchester by the Sea, Essex, 
Ipswich 
○ Salem Hub: Salem, Beverly, Peabody, Danvers 
○ Lynn Hub 
● Verification 
○ A concerned neighbor calls the statewide LUCE hotline and makes a report 
to a dispatcher. 
○ The dispatcher gets in contact with the appropriate LUCE hub. 
○ A trained verifier is given the caller’s description of what they saw and is 
dispatched to the scene.

○ Supporting neighbors affected by ICE detention with cash for housing,

Church. 
○ Also work with San Pedro/St. Peter’s in Salem to support those who call for

After the presentation, REC members had the opportunity to ask questions. Discussion 
focused on outreach to students at Salem State University and collaborations with the Race 
Equity Commission. There was also a question about how LUCE partners with local Police 
Departments; there is no formal relationship but there is a friendly informal relationship. 
 
6. Follow up on changes to the Discrimination Reporting Form. 
a. Discuss marketing campaign to distribute the form. 
 
IT needs some feedback on the requested changes to the Discrimination Reporting Form. 
Chair Zaragoza shared the following message from IT with items for the REC to consider 
and make decisions about. 
 
“To help move this forward and ensure I'm implementing the changes as intended, it would 
be helpful to get some additional detail on the following items: 
 
● Whether the disclaimer language should remain unchanged during consolidation, 
or if there are specific edits or revisions you would like incorporated as part of 
simplifying the language. 
● Which specific color style changes are being requested, particularly given that the 
current form was built using City-approved colors.  
● If the Type of Discrimination field is moved to an internal review step, whether 
routing the submission to you for categorization prior to continuing through the 
workflow is the appropriate process in light of the considerations outlined above. 
● Which field(s) specifically fall under the "unnecessary items" that can be deleted 
from the form.” 
 
Discussion among REC Members: 
● Categorization being an internal step, versus the submitters’ subjective selection of 
“Type of Discrimination” may require some additional work for staff or REC 
members, but is important to do. 
● Description should be required and add a sentence in the form instructions 
encouraging people to provide as much detail as possible.  
● There was emphasis among members that this has been a project being worked on 
for years and should be wrapped up soon, without significant work or costs. 
● Potentially explore other options for collecting submissions such as a Fillable PDF, 
Google Forms, Microsoft Forms, City Website Form Center, etc.  
● There was consensus among members that someone from the IT department should 
be invited to a future meeting to discuss this further.

7. New Business. 
a. September: Presentation to be determined – Shawn Newton from the Salem 
Race Equity Task Force. 
 
Vice Chair shared that Shawn Newton from the Salem Race Equity Task Force will be 
presenting at the meeting in September. He will share more background about this work 
and feedback that can inform the current Race Equity Commission members.  
 
No additional new business was presented. 
 
 
8. Adjournment. 
 
VOTE: Motion to adjourn was made by Rosa Alvarado, seconded by Lisa Cammarata , 
and the motion was approved unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 6:08 pm.

Samantha Giffen
